question: Does averaging trend signals over several horizons beat the core's two fixed horizons, robustly?
provenance: Multi-horizon averaging is standard in the trend-following literature (long-horizon cross-asset trend studies, managed-futures practice) as protection against horizon misspecification. Horizons are spaced x2-4 around the frozen ones; not tuned.
economics: canonical v3.1 with Binance funding, 20 bps
adoption_rule: ensemble Sharpe >= core Sharpe on both coin sets AND in both halves of each; otherwise keep the core
status_note: All data here has been seen; adoption would only create a forward candidate
